terms.gloss: I’m having a bad time; I’m in a bad way
evidence: Cic. Verr. 2.4.95: numquam tam male est Siculīs, quīn aliquid facētē et commodē dīcant (Lewis & Short s.v. facētus)
terms.comment: The opposite of mihi bene est: the dative of the person with the adverb, “it is badly with me”.

phrases.source: Libellus V, Lisbōna: castellum et ōceanārium

phrases.english: He’s having a good time by himself.

phrases.latin: malest, Cornificī, tuō Catullō, malest, mē hercule, et labōriōsē
phrases.english: your Catullus is not well, Cornificius, not well, by Hercules, and it’s hard going

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency: p. 109, checked against the searchable text of the book on 29 October 2026.
